title: The Loop
subtitle: Set it, live it, look at the tape

variants.anger: You have read about all of this before. You could explain the dichotomy of control to someone else, competently, and you still went off at your brother on Sunday.
variants.anxiety: You know, intellectually, that most of what you fear does not happen. Knowing it has never once helped at 3am.
variants.distraction: You have downloaded four apps to fix this. You used each one for about nine days.
variants.discipline: The problem was never that you did not know what to do. You have always known what to do.

cards.heading: Knowing is not the bottleneck
cards.body:
You do not have a knowledge problem. Everyone who reads Stoicism can recite it, and most of them still lose their temper in traffic.

The Stoics were not readers. They ran a loop, daily, for years.

cards.heading: The loop, in full
cards.body:
Morning: decide one thing you will hold to. Day: go out and fail at it in various interesting ways. Night: look at the tape without flinching.

The looking is not optional. Reps you never review are just movement.

quote.text: I will keep constant watch over myself and, most usefully, will put each day up for review.
quote.translation: Train, then check the tape. Every day, not when you feel like it.

cards.prompt: You set an intention this morning and broke it by 10am. What does the evening review do with that?

options.text: Records it plainly, and notes what was happening right before.
options.feedback: Correct. The breach is the data. What preceded it is the actual finding.

options.text: Skips it. Reviewing a bad day just makes you feel worse.
options.feedback: The days you want to skip are the only ones with anything in them.

options.text: Uses it to establish that you are not disciplined.
options.feedback: That is not review, that is a verdict on your character from a sample size of one.

cards.scenario: It is 11pm. You are tired, the day was mediocre, and you did not hold your intention. What does a trained person do?

options.text: Skip tonight and start properly tomorrow.
options.feedback: Tomorrow will also be tired. This is the exact move that ends every streak you have had.

options.text: Sixty seconds. What held, what ran me, done.
options.feedback: Yes. The review is meant to survive a bad day. That is the whole reason it is short.

options.text: Sit with it properly and write at length about what went wrong.
options.feedback: Admirable once. Unsustainable nightly, and a system you will not run is worth nothing.

cards.prompt: Pick one thing to hold to today. Then come back tonight for the Quench.
intentions: I will run the Quench tonight, even if the day was bad.
I will hold today's intention badly rather than not at all.
I will look at one thing honestly tonight that I would rather skip.
